subject: Service assurance tiers & volume discount structure
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sara Coleman <sara@nimbus.ai>, Jon Price <jon.price@nimbus.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Service assurance tiers & volume discount structure

Hi Sara / Jon,

Great meeting last week — thanks for walking through Nimbus's ingest-heavy use cases. Per our discussion I pulled together a concise proposal for our premium "Service Assurance" packaging so you can evaluate economics vs. self-hosting. High-level summary: 

- Bronze: 99.5% uptime / 8h business response / no dedicated on-call (best for non-prod).
- Silver: 99.9% uptime / 4h business response / shared on-call during extended hours.
- Premier: 99.95% uptime / 1h critical response / dedicated escalation coverage + quarterly runbooks.

Two commercial levers we highlighted: committed throughput discounts (monthly token/embedding commits) and an optional retainer for on-call coverage that offsets per-incident fees. I attached a PDF (Redwood_Premier_Tiers_v3.pdf) with the SKU table and example math.

Questions for you to help us finalize pricing:
1) Do you expect traffic to be spiky (bursty daily peaks) or steady high-throughput? That affects recommended commitment bands.
2) Is the core ask around latency SLA (1h incident response) or the escalation availability (24/7 vs extended hours)?
3) If we provide a 12-month commit, do you have target % discounts on incremental usage we should model?

Next step: if you can confirm the above, I'll loop in Laura (pricing) and Ben (finance) to produce a deal-level quote and a redlineable SOW.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: Redwood_Premier_Tiers_v3.pdf (PDF, 460KB)

From: Sara Coleman <sara@nimbus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Jon Price <jon.price@nimbus.ai>, procurement@nimbus.ai
Date: 2026-03-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service assurance tiers & volume discount structure

Karthik,

Thanks — the PDF helped. Quick clarifications before we move to an SOW draft:

- Traffic profile: bursty. We have large nightly inference windows and unpredictable spikes during batch jobs; peak tokens can be 4–5x baseline for 2–3 hours.
- Primary concern: predictable cost under spikes and a fast escalation path for production incidents (we can tolerate 4h for non-critical but need 1h for critical).
- Commercial ask: at scale, we've been quoted as high as 30% off list from other vendors for committed usage. Can Redwood model a similar tiered volume discount or an aggressive overage floor?

We also need clarity on what the "dedicated escalation coverage" means operationally (who is on-call, RTO, and how handoffs to our SREs work). Can the SOW outline escalation roster hours and on-call SLAs?

If you can draft an SOW with two options (Premier + 12-month commit; Premier + 24-month commit with deeper discounts), we can fast-track procurement.

—Sara
VP Product, Nimbus Analytics

On Thu, Mar 18, 2026 at 09:12 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> Great meeting last week — thanks for walking through Nimbus's ingest-heavy use cases.

Hi Sara — looping in Ben (finance) and Evelyn (technical account lead). Below are concrete options and the operational callouts that will go in the SOW. I've kept the math simple.

Option A — Premier | 12-mo commit
- Commit: 6B tokens/month equivalent (burst smoothing built-in)
- Price: $0.0012 / token (effective, after 18% commit discount)
- On-call retainer: $12,000 / month for guaranteed 1h critical response + 24/7 pager for severity-1
- Overage: billed at $0.0009 / token up to 150% of commit, then auto-scale pricing applies

Option B — Premier | 24-mo commit
- Commit: 6B tokens/month
- Price: $0.0010 / token (28% commit discount)
- On-call retainer: $10,000 / month (reduced due to longer commit)
- Overage: $0.0008 / token until 200% of commit

Operational SOW callouts we will include:
- Escalation roster: Redwood primary TAM (Evelyn) + on-call rotation; handoff window and runbook updates quarterly.
- RTO commitments: 1h initial response for Sev-1; 4h for Sev-2; detailed thresholds in SOW appendix.
- Incident bridge: Redwood will join customer bridge within 30 minutes of Sev-1 acknowledgment; we will provide post-incident RCA within 5 business days for Sev-1.

Ben: I left placeholders for exact legal language for credits; can you confirm the credit slab for 99.95 -> 99.90 and 99.9 -> 99.5?

Sara: I'll assemble an SOW draft with those two options and the pricing table attached. I'll also model a 30% volume discount scenario at 12-month and 24-month commits for comparison and mark it as an executive-level concession that requires approval.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Director, Partner Pricing — Redwood Inference

From: Sara Coleman <sara@nimbus.ai>

Date: 2026-03-30T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service assurance tiers & volume discount structure

Laura / Karthik — appreciate the detailed options. We reviewed internally and prefer Option B (24-mo commit) if you can confirm two items before procurement:

1) A 30% blended discount on committed usage for the first 12 months (applied to the first 6B tokens/month) — this is a key gating item for finance.
2) SOW to include explicit escalation playbook references: the onboarding work to add Redwood to our incident rotations and the cadence for joint tabletop exercises (quarterly).

If you can confirm those, we'll ask legal to route the SOW through procurement and target signature within 10 business days. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call this week to finalize.

—Sara
VP Product, Nimbus Analytics
